reference_modeling_code.detail: Publisher's runtime (Photon). Readable Python modeling, VAD head and pause segmenter; fused ops come from kestrel_kernels, which ships macOS arm64 wheels with a CPUKernelRuntime (smoke-tested 2026-10-04: get_runtime(cpu) and (mps) both load). transformers ParakeetForTDT is not used as an oracle.

model_card.detail: Languages, benchmark tables, long-form segmentation description; .eval_results/open_asr_leaderboard.yaml

key_fields.vad_head: proj Conv1d(1024->128,k1)+SiLU, ctx Conv1d(128->128,k5,pad2)+SiLU, out Conv1d(128->1,k1), sigmoid; input = subsampler output

dtype.evidence: config.dtype=float32 and both references (transformers ParakeetForTDT, kestrel load_model dtype=float32) compute in F32. Storage is mixed: every matmul/conv weight and the whole vad_head are F16 at rest (356 tensors), norms/biases/BN stats F32 (349). So the F32 GGUF is the parity artifact and an F16 GGUF is lossless at rest (F16 storage is the precision ceiling; the card's 'full precision' is not literal).

upstream_benchmarks.notes: Photon on NVIDIA GPU, Open ASR Leaderboard normalizer. v3 = 1.52 on same pipeline.
Uses Photon's VAD-head segmenter (<=30 s pause-cut segments). v3 = 2.71 via NeMo's long-audio path. Not comparable to a single-pass full-attention run.

reference_rationale: The publisher's runtime is the source of truth: every number on the card is Photon, which runs kestrel. kestrel owns the full pipeline we must reproduce: NeMo-style frontend (features.py), FastConformer + TDT greedy decode (model.py via kestrel_kernels CPUKernelRuntime), the vad_head forward (vad.py), and the long-form pause segmenter and segment stitching (segment.py, longform.py, runtime.py). It runs locally on CPU (kestrel 0.9.1 / kestrel-kernels 0.7.4, cp312 arm64). transformers ParakeetForTDT drops vad_head and is not used. NeMo cannot load this checkpoint (no .nemo).
known_risks: Long-form recipe is in scope and must match kestrel exactly: audio >30 s is cut at VAD-head pauses into <=30 s segments (no overlap, no context margins), each segment decoded independently, texts joined with a single space, timestamps shifted by segment start. Our parakeet runtime today runs the whole clip through one full-attention pass (max_audio_ms=0); ultra needs a new segmented path, gated on the presence of vad_head tensors.

vad_head.* (proj Conv1d 1024->128 k1 + SiLU, ctx Conv1d 128->128 k5 pad2 + SiLU, out Conv1d 128->1 k1, sigmoid) runs on the subsampler output only (post-linear, pre rel-pos/xscale/conformer). Needs converter support, GGUF tensors and a subsampler-only graph. kestrel scans in 120 s blocks; this is valid because the subsampler is local, but block-edge frames must match kestrel's per-block feature normalization.

Segmenter is host-side logic in kestrel/segment.py: speech = sigmoid >= 0.5 at 80 ms frames, bridge gaps <0.1 s, drop runs <0.1 s, pauses >=0.2 s, cut at midpoint of the last pause fully inside (1 s, 30 s), else midpoint-in-window, else hard cut at 30 s; segments with no speech are skipped; VAD scanned in 120 s blocks (valid because the subsampler is local). Stage 4 must reproduce this exactly for long-form parity.

Checkpoint is HF-transformers naming (encoder.subsampling.layers.*, self_attn.q_proj/relative_k_proj, decoder.lstm, joint.head, encoder_projector); scripts/convert-parakeet.py only reads NeMo state dicts. Needs an HF->NeMo key remap (or a transformers-input path) plus fused-joint handling.

Weights are F16 at rest despite config.dtype=float32. F32 GGUF is a pure upcast used for parity; F16 GGUF loses nothing at rest and is the natural shipping 'full' file. Quant WER deltas should be read against the F16 file, and F16-vs-F32 GGUF differences reflect ggml F16 compute only.
Same TDT joint/duration-head and FastConformer rel-pos risks as v3; language_detection is implicit (no LID tokens), inherited from v3.
Photon's per-segment output joins segment texts with a single space and shifts timestamps by segment start; segment-boundary punctuation/casing may differ from a single-pass decode.

Per-feature normalization is computed per call in kestrel: the VAD scan normalizes over each 120 s block, while ASR normalizes over each segment. Our frontend must reproduce both scopes; normalizing over the whole file would shift VAD probabilities and segment features.

kestrel is the oracle but runs fused kestrel_kernels ops (CPUKernelRuntime). Tensor dumps need hooks around kestrel modules rather than a transformers-style output_hidden_states; check CPU vs CUDA kernel numerics before treating CPU dumps as ground truth for the card's GPU numbers.

Short-clip behavior: clips that fit in 30 s bypass VAD and segmentation entirely (fits_one_segment), so LibriSpeech/FLEURS never exercise the new path; a dedicated long-form set (card: TED-LIUM 3, 11 talks) is required for acceptance.
